title: Director, Learning & Development, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need.

As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at ScholarRock.com and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn.

Summary of Position:

We are seeking a strategic and results-driven Director, Learning & Development – EMEA to lead the development and execution of learning initiatives across EMEA markets.

This role will focus on strengthening organizational capabilities across three key pillars: Clinical Acumen, Business Acumen, and Leadership & Soft Skills, ensuring employees have the knowledge, skills, and confidence to drive business performance.

The Director will partner closely with regional leadership and global cross-functional teams to deliver a consistent global learning strategy while addressing local market needs.


Position Responsibilities

Clinical Acumen & Scientific Excellence

  • Develop learning programs focused on disease state, mechanisms of action, clinical evidence, and therapeutic landscapes. Enhancing clinical story telling consistent with the approved product information (SmPC) and applicable codes of practice. Partner and coordinate with Commercial, Medical Affairs, Marketing, and other stakeholders to ensure scientific knowledge and learning standards are met. L&D drives design, delivery and measurement of training programs, and collaborates with functional leads on application in the field.
    • Establish clinical competency assessments and certification programs, defined jointly with Medical Affairs and the Information Officer / Scientific Service, to ensure readiness and proficiency and to meet national requirements for medical sales representative qualification where applicable.

      • Business Acumen & Commercial Excellence

      • Build capabilities in market understanding, strategic thinking, business planning, and commercial execution.
      • Develop learning initiatives that strengthen top-quality customer engagement, account management, and competitive understanding.
      • Partner with regional leaders to identify capability gaps and align learning priorities with business objectives.
      • Support product launches, commercial readiness, and continuous performance improvement.

        • Leadership Development & Soft Skills

        • Design programs focused on emotional intelligence, communication, effective questioning, active listening, and influencing skills.
        • Strengthen leadership capabilities in coaching, feedback, accountability, and team development.
        • Foster collaboration, adaptability, and a culture of continuous learning.
        • Integrate behavioral development into clinical and commercial learning initiatives.

          • Global Alignment & Learning Effectiveness

          • Translate the Global L&D strategy into a regional learning roadmap aligned with European business priorities.
          • Ensure consistency in learning objectives, content, competency standards, and execution across markets.
          • Adapt learning experiences to local market requirements while maintaining global alignment.
          • Implement learning assessments, certification, and performance measurement to demonstrate impact.
          • In line with Company policies, leverage Artificial Intelligence and digital learning platforms and innovative methodologies to enhance learning effectiveness.
          • Ensure that the use of AI and digital tools for content creation maintains the required medical, legal and compliance review standards, data privacy and traceability.

            • Medical, Legal & Compliance Governance

            In Europe, learning operates within a highly regulated framework. The Director will establish and run a structured governance and operating model with Medical Affairs and the Information Officer / Scientific Service on one side, and Legal & Compliance on the other. This model ensures that all scientific and medical training content is accurate, balanced and approved through the appropriate channels, and that all learning, especially for customer-facing roles, meets applicable legal, regulatory and industry code requirements.

          • Build and maintain a formal operating model with Medical Affairs, the Information Officer / Scientific Service and Legal & Compliance, defining roles, responsibilities and decision rights (e.g. RACI) for how training content is developed, reviewed, approved, delivered and updated.
          • Co-develop scientific and medical curricula with Medical Affairs as scientific content owner, with L&D accountable for instructional design, delivery, assessment and learning effectiveness.
          • Ensure all training materials go through the applicable medical, legal and regulatory review and approval process before use, with version control, expiry and withdrawal management.
          • Partner with Legal & Compliance to design and deliver mandatory training on industry codes (EFPIA and national codes of practice), HCP/HCO interactions, promotional and non-promotional activities, anti-bribery and corruption and data privacy.
          • Maintain complete, audit-ready training records and certifications to support internal audits, regulatory inspections and code-of-practice enquiries.
          • Agree country-level adaptations (if any) with local Medical, Information Officer and Legal & Compliance leads, ensuring national requirements are met while global standards are maintained.

    Candidate Requirements
    • Degree in Life Sciences, Business, Education, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
    • 8–10+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including Learning & Development, commercial training, or capability development.
    • Experience in field-based teams’ training, both commercial and medical is essential
    • Strong clinical and commercial acumen, preferably within specialty pharmaceuticals or rare diseases.
    • Experience developing and implementing learning strategies across European markets.
    • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and collaborate across global, regional, and local teams.
    • Strong leadership, facilitation, communication, and project management skills.
    • Experience with learning technologies, competency frameworks, and certification programs.
    • Solid understanding of the European pharmaceutical regulatory and compliance environment, including the EFPIA Code, national codes of practice and the role of the Information Officer / Scientific Service.
      • Proven experience working within medical, legal and regulatory review and approval processes for training materials.
      • Track record of building effective operating models with Medical Affairs and Legal & Compliance.
      • Fluency in English; additional European languages preferred.
      • Ability to travel up to 50%

        • Success Measures

        • Improved clinical knowledge, business acumen, and behavioral competencies.
        • Consistent execution of global learning standards across European markets.
        • Demonstrated employee readiness through assessments and certification.
        • Audit- and inspection-ready training documentation.
        • Strong alignment between learning initiatives and regional business priorities.
        • Clear, agreed governance with Medical Affairs, the Information Officer / Scientific Service and Legal & Compliance.
        • Measurable improvements in individual capabilities and organizational performance.

title: Director of Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Our Story Hello there. We’re Zopa. We started our journey back in 2005, building the first ever peer-to-peer lending company. Fast forward to 2020 and we launched Zopa Bank. A bank that listens to what our customers don’t like about finance and does the opposite. We’re redefining what it feels like to work in finance. Our vision for a new era of banking puts people front and centre — we’ve built a business that empowers everyone to aim high, every day, to move finance forward. Find out more about our fantastic offerings at Zopa.com! We’re incredibly proud of our achievements and none of it would be possible without the amazing team here. It’s not just industry awards we’re winning, we’ve also been named in the top three UK’s Most Loved Workplaces. If you embrace unconventional challenges, are unafraid to think differently and are driven to make an outsized impact, you’ll thrive here at Zopa, so join us, and make it count. Want to see us in action? Follow us on Instagram @zopalife

As a Director of Engineering, you’ll lead an established engineering organisation responsible for one of our key business areas, with the autonomy and accountability to make a significant impact on how engineering performs at Zopa. You’ll set direction, build high-performing teams and drive meaningful improvements across people, technology and ways of working. This isn’t a role focused on incremental change: we’re looking for someone who can identify where the biggest opportunities exist, create a clear strategy and turn it into measurable progress. You’ll have the scope to influence significant technical and architectural decisions, improve engineering effectiveness and shape how we build and operate technology.

Your impact will extend beyond the teams you directly lead. Our Directors are expected to raise the level of engineering across Zopa, working closely with Product, Commercial and Technology leaders to turn engineering improvements into better business outcomes. You’ll bring strong people leadership, technical credibility and a genuinely data-led approach to understanding what’s working and where we can improve, while helping us push further in areas such as AI-enabled engineering.

This is an opportunity for an experienced engineering leader to take real ownership, drive substantial change and clearly see the results of the decisions they make.

As a highly collaborative role, you’ll attend our Canary Wharf office 3 days per week


What you'll do:
  • Lead Engineering Strategy & Drive Meaningful Change:
  • Set and lead the engineering strategy for your area, identifying the biggest opportunities to improve technology, people and ways of working.
  • Take ownership of moving the organisation from its current state towards a clear future state, building stakeholder buy-in and delivering measurable progress.
  • Operate with a high degree of autonomy, making decisions and driving execution without requiring significant direction.
  • Build a High-Performing Engineering Organisation:
  • Lead a sizeable engineering organisation through Engineering Managers, setting a high bar for people leadership and engineering performance.
  • Build and develop high-performing teams through effective hiring, performance management and people practices.
  • Identify organisational challenges and opportunities, including how teams are structured and how engineering capacity is used most effectively.
  • Reduce key-person dependencies and build an organisation that can perform sustainably as it evolves.
  • Improve Engineering Effectiveness Through Data & AI:
  • Identify and deliver improvements that make engineers and engineering teams more effective across people, technology and process.
  • Use meaningful engineering metrics to identify opportunities, guide decisions and demonstrate whether changes are delivering the intended impact.
  • Drive practical adoption and experimentation with AI, focusing on how it changes engineering effectiveness rather than simply introducing new tools.
  • Share meaningful evidence of engineering performance with teams and stakeholders to inform decisions and drive continuous improvement.
  • Shape Technology & Architecture:
  • Bring the technical credibility to challenge significant design and architectural decisions and make informed judgements on complex technology choices.
  • Develop clear strategies for improving, modernising, consolidating or replacing technology where opportunities exist.
  • Make pragmatic build, buy or partner decisions based on the needs of the organisation.
  • Work effectively with engineering, architecture, platform and other technology teams to manage dependencies and deliver change.
  • Partner Across the Business & Raise the Engineering Bar:
  • Build strong partnerships with Product and Commercial leaders, creating shared ownership of outcomes rather than operating in functional silos.
  • Influence senior stakeholders, navigate demanding conversations and build support for significant engineering change.
  • Build effective relationships across Technology and supporting functions, understanding how to leverage those teams rather than simply transact with them.
  • Contribute beyond your immediate organisation, helping raise the level of engineering across Zopa.

    • How you'll do it:
  • Lead with Autonomy & Ownership:
  • Bring the experience to quickly understand the problem space, form a clear point of view and turn it into action.
  • Take ownership of outcomes, moving at pace while knowing when to seek input, support or validation.
  • Draw on lessons from challenges you’ve faced before, adapting your approach rather than relying on a fixed playbook.
  • Be Curious, Adaptable & Improvement-Focused:
  • Ask the right questions, challenge existing approaches and continually look for opportunities to make engineering better.
  • Stay adaptable as business priorities and technology needs evolve, responding effectively when plans need to change.
  • Bring genuine curiosity to emerging technologies, particularly AI, and be willing to experiment, learn and apply what works.
  • Use Data to Make Better Decisions:
  • Take a genuinely data-led approach, using meaningful metrics to understand engineering performance and identify where improvement is needed.
  • Go beyond reporting metrics by using them to shape priorities, change behaviours and measure the impact of your decisions.
  • Communicate engineering effectiveness in a way that gives teams and senior stakeholders a clear view of progress and outcomes.
  • Influence with High EQ & Low Ego:
  • Build trusted relationships across Engineering, Product, Commercial and the wider organisation.
  • Be comfortable having difficult conversations, constructively challenging others and standing behind decisions you believe are right.
  • Adapt your style to different stakeholders, combining conviction with collaboration to build buy-in and move change forward.
  • Think Big & Deliver at Pace:
  • Look beyond incremental improvements and identify opportunities to make a step change in the organisations you lead.
  • Translate ambitious ideas into practical plans, bringing people with you and creating momentum towards meaningful outcomes.
  • Balance long-term thinking with visible progress, demonstrating impact while building towards larger-scale change.

    • About you:
  • You’re an experienced engineering leader who has led sizeable teams and knows how to build a high-performing organisation through strong Engineering Managers, effective hiring, performance management and people leadership.
  • You can demonstrate meaningful improvements to engineering effectiveness across people, technology and ways of working. You use data and metrics to identify opportunities, make decisions and understand whether your changes are having the intended impact.
  • You’ve led significant organisational change, taking teams from their current state to a materially better one. You can set a clear direction, build stakeholder buy-in and translate strategy into tangible progress.
  • You bring the technical credibility to engage in significant design and architectural decisions. You can process complex information, challenge thinking and make sound judgements, including practical build, buy or partner decisions.
  • You know how to build strong partnerships with Product and influence senior stakeholders. You’re comfortable navigating competing priorities and difficult conversations, combining conviction with high EQ and a low-ego approach.
  • You’re actively exploring how AI can improve engineering effectiveness and can talk practically about what you’ve tried, what worked, what didn’t and what you learned.
  • You’re comfortable operating with significant autonomy, bringing experience and judgement to complex challenges without needing the path laid out for you. You’re naturally curious, adaptable and resilient, and comfortable adjusting course as priorities change.
  • Experience within FinTech, lending or another regulated environment would be valuable, as would experience in a technology-first organisation.

    • At Zopa we value flexible ways of working.

    We value face-to-face collaboration and a good work-life balance. This hybrid role requires you to come to our London office 2-3 days a week.

    You'll also have the option of working from abroad for up to 120 days a year!* But no matter where you are, we’ll make sure you’ve got everything you need to thrive, both in your work and home life, from day one.

    *Subject to having the right to work in the country of choice

    Diversity Statement

    Zopa is proud to offer a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds leads to better products for our customers and a unique company culture for our people. We are made up of nearly 50 nationalities, have a DE&I forum made up of Zopians wanting to make a difference and we are proud of our culture where everyone can bring their full self to work. Our approach to DE&I is reflected in our hiring process so please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments.

    Our approach to AI in interviews

    At Zopa, AI isn't something we're testing out — it's part of how we work every day. As a proud partner of Jobs 2030, we're committed to building AI fluency across our workforce, and we expect Zopians to use AI as part of how they do their jobs.

    Because of that, we want to be transparent about how we think about AI use during our hiring process.

    Behavioural and competency-based interviews: please don't use AI. These conversations are designed to understand you — your experiences, your judgment, and how you've approached real situations. An AI-generated answer can't tell us that. What it can do is get in the way of us finding out whether we're the right fit for each other.

    Technical interviews: it depends on the role. Some technical stages actively welcome AI use, others don't. Your Talent Partner will let you know what's expected at each stage. Where AI is part of the assessment, we'll be interested not just in the outcome, but in how you used it – the tools you chose, your reasoning, and the decisions you made along the way.

title: Director of Indirect Procurement and Logistics (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
Mission Brief 

Build the physical and commercial infrastructure that allows launch cadence to scale. This Director leads procurement of launch pads, test and production infrastructure and other indirect spend, and owns internal logistics and international transport across the operating network. The role must turn project requirements into executable contracts and ensure flight hardware reaches each next operation in the right condition, with full visibility and traceability. 

Your Role in Our Space Mission: 

  • Launch and industrial infrastructure: Own the commercial procurement strategy for new launch pads, test facilities, factory expansion, production equipment and supporting utilities. With the project sponsor and technical authority, package the work, test the market, establish realistic lead times and secure suppliers capable of delivering the required capacity. 
  • Project procurement and contracts: Lead tenders, supplier evaluation, negotiations and contract award within delegated authority. Set schedule, acceptance, warranty and change control terms that support the project delivery plan. Manage commercial performance, claims and supplier escalation through commissioning and handover, working with Engineering, Facilities, Legal and Finance. 
  • Indirect spend: Own sourcing and purchasing for non production goods and services, including facilities, site services, IT, professional services and operational equipment. Build category plans and appropriate approvals, with clear visibility of committed spend and contract obligations. 
  • International logistics network: Design and operate the movement of parts and flight hardware from suppliers into Munich, engines to Sweden for test and back to Germany for integration, and integrated vehicles and support equipment onward to launch sites. Establish route capacity, freight partners, packaging, customs processes, permits and contingency options ahead of the production ramp. 
  • Internal material flow: Own goods receipt, storage, inventory control, kitting, line feeding and physical transfers within production and integration sites. Set handling, preservation and traceability standards for high value flight hardware, and scale the warehouse and material flow model with output.

title: Engineering Lead
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

We’re an AI-first business, so whatever the role, we want people who reach for AI by default, stay curious about what it can do, and use it to work faster and think bigger.

THE ROLE

Engineering Lead for the Acquisition team. You’ll report to our Head of Engineering. You’ll work closely with the PM to lead the team toward its goals, owning delivery, operational reliability and developer experience. You’ll ship production code and provide technical coaching and leadership to the engineers around you, not line management. You’ll also shape how the team uses AI tools and coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

WHAT WE THINK IS MOST EXCITING ABOUT THE ROLE:

Lead a team building products that directly drive Flock’s growth

  • Own delivery and technical quality for the Acquisition team, working hand in hand with the PM to ship features that directly impact how fleets find and choose Flock.

  • Write high-quality, well-tested TypeScript and own end-to-end delivery to production

Partner with product to drive impact

  • Work closely with the PM, the Engineering Leadership Team and stakeholders to translate business goals into clear technical scope, success metrics and delivery plans.

Grow engineers around you

  • Lead by example through code, design discussions and pairing.

  • Coach and mentor engineers across the team to raise standards and share ownership of technical direction.

Shape how the team works, not just what it builds

  • Drive improvements to developer experience, CI/CD, observability and release practices that make the whole team faster and more confident.

  • Make pragmatic trade-offs that balance reliability, performance and cost across AWS services.

  • Decide how the team uses AI, from coding assistants to agent workflows in review and release, keeping engineering judgement where it matters.

Curious how we build the future of fleet insurance? Dive into our Product & Engineering Blog, packed with technical deep-dives, behind-the-scenes stories, and real insights from the team you’d be joining.

A LITTLE MORE ON WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

As an Engineering Lead at Flock you’ll own delivery and technical direction for the Acquisition team, co-leading with the PM to ship products that directly drive growth, while raising the bar for the engineers around you.

API-Driven Development

  • Integrate with and contribute to the development of RESTful APIs exposed via API Gateway.

Serverless & Cloud Infrastructure

  • Use your AWS experience (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) to support and extend the Acquisition team’s services and pipelines.

  • Work with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform or CDK for provisioning and managing cloud resources.

Collaboration & Agile Delivery

  • Co-own the team’s success with the PM, jointly leading projects from scoping and planning through to delivery and measuring impact.

  • Give engineers the space and ownership to lead projects themselves, asking the right questions to challenge their thinking and help them land on the right solution.

Code Quality & Technical Standards

  • Deliver high-quality, well-tested code and act as a force-multiplier, raising standards through code reviews, pairing and design discussions.

  • Champion practical testing, type-safe APIs and pragmatic patterns that shape long-term technical direction across the team.

  • Set the example on AI-assisted development and coach engineers on where it genuinely speeds the team up and where human judgement needs to stay in the loop.

Working closely with your PM, you’ll bring clarity to complex problems and help define sharply scoped, impactful deliverables. Your success won’t be measured by your own output alone, but by the output, quality and growth of the whole team around you.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FLOCK:

ESSENTIAL

  • Proven ability to co-lead a team alongside a PM, taking joint ownership of delivery, quality and outcomes, not just your own output.

  • Strong hands-on engineering ability; comfortable shipping high-quality, well-tested TypeScript in production and holding the team to the same standard.

  • Significant experience with AWS and modern serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) or other cloud platforms.

  • A pragmatic approach to technical decisions, balancing reliability, observability, performance and cost, and bringing engineers along on the reasoning.

  • Track record of raising engineering standards as a force-multiplier, through code reviews, pairing, design discussions and shaping long-term technical direction.

  • Strong communication skills; able to represent the team upwards and translate business goals into clear technical scope and delivery plans.

  • Experience improving developer experience, CI/CD, release practices and delivery cadence across a team.

  • Confident using AI development tools every day, with experience of helping a team adopt them without letting quality slip.

PREFERABLE

  • Experience aligning technical direction beyond your immediate team, working with senior stakeholders and other leads to shape how engineering works at a broader level.

  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform or CDK, with a track record of improving operational resilience through observability, runbooks and automated recovery.

  • Practical experience designing event-driven, distributed systems and navigating the trade-offs that come with eventual consistency at scale.

  • Background in a fast-moving, product-led environment where commercial impact drives decisions and adapting quickly is part of the job.

  • A track record of creating the conditions for engineers to step up, not just mentoring but actively giving ownership and space to grow.

WHAT WE OFFER (in addition to a competitive salary)

  • 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖

  • Share Incentive Plan 📈

  • Workplace Pension 💰

  • Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options)

  • Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵

  • Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣

  • £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓

  • £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

  • 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. Visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days.

ONE LAST THING..

Authenticity is important to us. We value the unique qualities and experiences you bring. So if you apply, just be your genuine self. It’s who we want!

title: Engineering Manager - BCP Content stream (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Notre équipe BCP (Business Capabilities Platform) recherche un·e Engineering Manager (f/m/d) en CDI, basé·e à Lille - Upline.

Qui sommes-nous ? L'équipe Content est au cœur de la stratégie d'expérience globale de Decathlon. Notre mission est de propulser et de diffuser l'ensemble des contenus de l'écosystème : de la gestion des médias à l'internationalisation des traductions, en passant par la valorisation des avis utilisateurs. Nous gérons des plateformes à très haute échelle, connectées mondialement, avec pour ambition de transformer la manière dont nos utilisateurs consomment et interagissent avec l'information produit. Un terrain de jeu technologique et fonctionnel passionnant, multiculturel et à fort impact !

TA FUTURE CONTRIBUTION

En tant qu'Engineering Manager, tu seras le pilier humain et technique d'une équipe de 13 ingénieur·es (développeur·ses, QA, support), composée de profils internes et de partenaires externes. Ton rôle combinera le leadership de personnes, le cadrage de domaines fonctionnels variés et la gouvernance technologique.

  • Management & Accompagnement : Tu animes, coaches et fais grandir une équipe pluridisciplinaire. Tu insuffles une culture de collaboration, d'amélioration continue et d'excellence d'ingénierie, tout en gérant la relation avec nos partenaires externes.

  • Stratégie Produit & Déploiement : Tu pilotes le déploiement à l'échelle de onecontent comme produit de diffusion unique des contenus de Decathlon, avant de mener la redéfinition globale de notre stratégie de plateforme.

  • Innovation & IA : Tu orchestres la construction et le déploiement de Onetranslate, notre moteur de traduction de pointe piloté par l'Intelligence Artificielle.

  • Expérience Utilisateur : Tu supervises le déploiement du nouveau moteur de modération des avis clients, incluant la gestion et la valorisation des avis photos.

  • Gouvernance Technique : Sans être nécessairement 100% les mains dans le code au quotidien, tu es le garant de la cohérence technique. Tu challenges les architectures proposées par l'équipe, orientes les choix technologiques et restes prêt·e à faire du hands-on si la situation le demande.

CE QUE TU APPORTES

  • Une première expérience réussie en management d'équipe technique (Engineering Management, Lead Dev, ou Tech Lead), qui te permet de savoir cadrer et soutenir des équipes travaillant sur des domaines fonctionnels et des cycles de vie différents.

  • Une forte sensibilité d'architecture logicielle : tu es capable de challenger des patterns complexes (microservices, event-driven architecture, streaming de données) et de dialoguer d'égal à égal avec des expert·es techniques.

  • Une culture axée sur la livraison de valeur ("Delivery Focus") et la robustesse des plateformes à forte charge.

  • Un excellent relationnel, de l'empathie, et une capacité à naviguer dans un écosystème de plateforme internationale (anglais courant indispensable).

STACK TECHNIQUE

  • Backend : Java, Spring Boot

  • Frontend : React, Next.js

  • Bases de données : PostgreSQL, MongoDB

  • Événements / CI-CD : Kafka, GitHub Actions

CE QUE NOUS T’OFFRONS

  • Organisation de travail hybride ;

  • Matériel fourni en accord avec tes missions et nos engagements sociétaux (Mac ou Windows) ;

  • Une équipe de projet locale au sein d'un réseau mondial (possibilité de carrière internationale) ;

  • Développement des compétences et accompagnement (diversité des projets, formations internes et externes, etc.) ;

  • Package de rémunération (actionnariat salarié, bonus mensuels/trimestriels).

NOTRE ENGAGEMENT EN FAVEUR DE L'INCLUSION ET DE L'ACCESSIBILITE

Chez Decathlon, nous reconnaissons l'immense valeur qu'apporte la diversité à nos équipes et nous nous efforçons continuellement de favoriser et de cultiver un lieu de travail inclusif et équitable : c'est pourquoi l'Inclusion est l'un de nos Fondamentaux Humains. Nous encourageons les personnes de tous horizons et de toutes capacités à postuler, car nous sommes convaincu·es que la diversité des pensées, des cultures, des identités et des expériences vécues nous rend plus fort·es. Decathlon s'engage également à offrir un processus de sélection inclusif et accessible à tous les candidat·es. En cas de besoin d'aménagement, tu peux en faire la demande via le formulaire de candidature, celle-ci sera confidentielle. Ces demandes n'affectent pas le résultat du processus de recrutement.

DECATHLON DIGITAL 

Imaginez si la technologie nous permettait de repousser les frontières et d'offrir des expériences sportives inédites. C'est précisément notre ambition chez Decathlon Digital ! Nous sommes une équipe de plus de 5 000 experts en ingénierie logicielle, gestion de produits, données, cloud et cybersécurité, répartis à Paris, Lille et Amsterdam. Ensemble, nous créons la plus vaste plateforme sportive numérique, en exploitant les innovations technologiques pour optimiser la chaîne de valeur, concevoir des expériences connectées et donner une seconde vie à nos produits.

Changeons la donne pour de bon. Notre passion du sport nous guide et nous voulons qu’elle perdure. C’est pourquoi nous nous engageons à bâtir un modèle technologique plus durable, en réduisant notre impact direct sur l'environnement, et en créant un espace sûr et inclusif pour apprendre et nous épanouir ensemble. Rejoins l’équipe et façonnons le futur du sport.

title: Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us. 

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

📍London or Remote (UK) | 💰 Base salary for this role is £112,000 - £145,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits 

Engineering Management at Monzo:

Engineering Managers at Monzo are part of cross-functional, autonomous teams and groups. Our teams are mission driven, and typically include Product Managers, backend, web and mobile engineers as well as data scientists, designers and subject matter experts relevant to that mission. Teams are organised into groups, and then collectives - we aim to keep our line management structure as shallow as possible, and for teams to directly own decision making relevant to their work.

The Engineering Manager role at Monzo is split into three pillars - people, product, and technical leadership. Engineering Managers are accountable for the technical and delivery outcomes for their area - that means supporting and developing best in class engineering talent, as well as creating an inclusive team environment for people to do their best work.

You can read more on the expectations of Engineering Managers on our Progression Framework.

The Role

We're continuously hiring Engineering Managers as we continue to grow and build new teams. We hire on a pipeline based approach which means your application will be considered across all of our open EM positions. We use the interview process to assess your strengths and we'll match you to a role that best aligns with your experience. Of course, this is a collaborative process so you can also tell us which roles you're most interested in as you progress through interviews 😊 We're currently hiring across Platform, Core App, and Expansion.

You’ll spend your time:

  • Taking accountability for delivery across your squad(s), collaborating with the Technical Lead and Product Manager.
  • Actively fostering a high bar for engineering excellence within your teams. You’re accountable for the technical outcomes your teams deliver alongside individual engineer performance and growth, so holding a high bar (and clearly articulating your expectations) is key.
  • You’ll initially lead a group of around 7-10 engineers (depending on the role) and support, coach and develop them through their career with regular 1:1s and continuous feedback.
  • Partner with senior engineers in your area to drive technical initiatives that raise the bar for our engineering practices.
  • Lead on communication with stakeholders from other teams, creating focus space for engineers to do their best work.
  • Collaborate with the wider engineering organisation to contribute to company-wide best managerial and technical practices and standards.

You should apply if:

While this is not a role which requires hands-on-coding, we are looking for an experienced manager who has a strong technical and delivery background and has worked as a software engineer in previous roles.

We recognise that engineering managers lead in different ways, we’re looking for someone who: 

  • Is comfortable operating with ambiguous problem areas with a high degree of autonomy.
  • It’s a bonus if you have experience working in an experimentation led environment.
  • Has delivery experience and is able to guide the squads in achieving their outcomes.
  • Focuses on outcomes over processes, who optimises for the highest impact and leverage.
  • Is able to input, understand and challenge engineering decisions - but to empower the team to make those decisions themselves
  • Has an understanding of what good looks like for a high-performing team of engineers and ability to chart a course to get there
  • Is able to to coach people to achieve their goals
  • Has a natural ability to inspire and motivate a team

We consider your application across all open EM roles at Monzo independent of which role you've applied for, so if you've recently applied to a similar role at Monzo and have been unsuccessful, please wait 6 months before applying again.

How we work 💻:

Locations & Flexible Working : 

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. 

We value meeting in person but there’s no pressure to come into the office, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨

Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.

Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life.

At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance. 

You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨

Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼

The interview process:

After an initial informal 30 min recruiting call, our interview process involves two main stages:

  1. Initial Call Interview (1 hour) You'll meet with one of our Senior Engineering Managers or Engineering Directors. They'll ask you about your previous experience, in particular people leadership, product delivery and technical leadership. They’ll ask example based questions (‘Tell me about a time when…’)

  2. Loop Stage (3 hours 30 mins) The Loop stage consists of 3 x 60 min interviews that take place over 1-2 days (depending on your availability) and one 30 minute reverse interview (more details below).

The Loop is one stage, and the interviews in the Loop are:

- Team and Org Management (1 hour)
An example based interview with 1-2 of our engineering leaders. They’re interested to hear examples from your previous experience on the teams you’ve led, how you’ve shaped and partnered with product, and the impact you had.

- System Design (1 hour)
You'll partner with a Staff or Principal Engineer on a technical whiteboarding exercise.

- Behavioural (1 hour)
Similar to Team and Org Management, this is an example based interview with 1-2 Engineering Leaders. This interview focuses on your people leadership style and core behaviours as an Engineering Manager.

descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

You will own our Kubernetes product end to end: a metal-to-on-demand platform built on in-house infrastructure, with GPU support for training, inference, and general-purpose compute.

Kubernetes is our product, not just our platform — we run it on infrastructure we own end to end. You will decide how the control plane scales, how GPUs get scheduled, and how quickly a rack of bare metal becomes an on-demand cluster a customer can use. The decisions you make here shape how our infrastructure scales from today's footprint to a gigawatt, and how we turn frontier AI research into production systems used by millions.

This is a role for an engineer who leads from the front because that is where the work is, not because management was the next rung on the ladder.

What You Will Do

  • Design and ship the control plane. You build alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions — scheduling, operators, provisioning, node lifecycle.

  • Grow the engineers, not just the software. You set the standard for ownership, remove the obstacles in their way, and coach them past their comfort zone until the work they ship surprises them.

  • Own the reliability of the Kubernetes control plane. It is the team's headline KPI. You make the calls when it breaks at 3am, and your engineers learn from how you do it.

  • Shrink the distance from metal to on-demand. Provisioning a cluster should be minutes of automation, not weeks of tickets.

  • Partner with Product Managers to set priorities, scope initiatives, and make the technical and business tradeoffs.

  • Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback — the leadership work that never becomes someone else's job.

  • Define the team's processes and execution rituals as it grows.

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • You have run Kubernetes in anger — and ideally built parts of it: operators, schedulers, controllers. You understand what happens underneath it, and you have worked on Linux directly, not just on managed services that sit on top of it.

  • You have run GPU workloads on Kubernetes, or you are confident you can own that domain fast.

  • You think like a developer who happens to build infrastructure, not an operator who manages it. You write code other engineers depend on.

  • Extensive experience building backend or infrastructure systems.

  • You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

title: Engineering Technician
descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

 

YOUR IMPACT

At Proxima Fusion, we're developing the world's leading stellarator technology. To turn cutting-edge designs into reality, we need skilled technicians who can bring complex, first-of-a-kind hardware to life. As a Technician at Proxima Fusion, you'll work hands-on with Proxima-designed components, magnets, mechanical assemblies and other critical systems, supporting their build, assembly, integration and testing.

Working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, you'll help turn ambitious designs into reliable hardware, solve practical challenges on the shop floor and contribute to developing the processes and tooling needed to build Alpha. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced engineering and hands-on manufacturing, helping build one of Europe's most ambitious engineering projects.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Build, assemble and modify prototypes, experimental hardware, custom tooling and development rigs for engineering and special projects across the programme.

  • Turn engineering drawings, models, and sketches into practical hardware. Clarify missing requirements and agree the build approach with the responsible engineer before committing to uncertain or irreversible steps.

  • Fabricate and adapt components using fitting, cutting, drilling, soldering, bonding and assembly techniques within your competence. Coordinate specialist machining, welding or other work when needed.

  • Identify buildability issues early, including tolerance stacks, inaccessible fasteners, component fit and assembly sequence, and provide practical feedback to the design team.

  • Prepare and run development trials, including winding, joining, insulation and impregnation trials as assigned. Install instrumentation, commission rigs with engineers, take measurements and record what changed and what happened.

  • Investigate unexpected behaviour, propose practical fixes and work through build-test-modify iterations with engineers.

  • Organise the practical delivery of assigned projects: source small parts and consumables through agreed purchasing routes, arrange tools and build activities, and keep the workshop ready for use. Communicate progress, blockers and changing priorities to the lead technician.

  • Keep clear as-built records, annotated drawings, photographs, settings and trial observations so another technician can reproduce the work and understand each modification.

  • Transfer proven prototypes and methods to manufacturing or routine testing through initial work instructions, tooling, assembly sequences, training and technical handovers.

  • Work with engineers to identify hazards and establish the necessary risk assessments and controls before starting work on unproven hardware.

     

WHO YOU ARE

  • A technical apprenticeship or vocational qualification in mechanical, electrical, mechatronic or related engineering work, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • Hands-on experience building, modifying and troubleshooting mechanical or electromechanical hardware in a workshop, laboratory, development or advanced manufacturing environment.

  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, tolerances and 3D models, with working familiarity with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and practical measurement skills.

  • Confident hand-tool and workshop skills, sound fabrication and assembly judgement, and a willingness to develop unfamiliar techniques.

  • Resourcefulness with incomplete information: you investigate, ask useful questions, find suitable parts and propose a practical next step while keeping the engineering objective clear.

  • Sound judgement about technical uncertainty, safety and when a build or design change requires engineering review before proceeding.

  • The ability to organise work, adapt to agreed priority changes and document configurations and findings clearly.

  • Working English for technical discussions, drawings, instructions and build records.

Nice to have

  • Specialist fabrication skills such as manual or CNC machining, sheet-metal work, welding, brazing or additive manufacturing.

  • Experience creating or modifying simple parts and fixtures in CATIA, SolidWorks, Fusion 360 or similar CAD tools.

  • Experience with instrumentation, sensors, data acquisition, electrical wiring, vacuum, cryogenics or superconducting hardware.

  • Experience with composites, resins, vacuum bagging, insulation or impregnation.

  • Experience taking first-of-a-kind hardware or a prototype process through to repeatable manufacturing and technical handover.

  • German language skills.

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

 

This job would require frequent travels to our office in Villigen ( Zurich, CH)

title: Field Account Executive - Bonn / Ruhrgebiet (w/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über uns & Die Opportunity

Bereit für die Freiheit, komplett eigenständig zu arbeiten, aber mit der Power eines globalen Tech-Pioniers im Rücken?
Lightspeed ist die führende All-in-One-Plattform für Handel und Gastronomie. Als KI-getriebenes Tech-Unternehmen bieten wir dir eines der besten SaaS-Produkte auf dem Markt.

In dieser Rolle bist du nicht einfach nur Angestellter – du bist der "Owner" deines eigenen Gebiets in Bonn oder Ruhrgebiet. Gemeinsam mit einem neuen, dynamischen Team von ca. 8 Personen und einem erfahrenen Manager vor Ort eroberst du den Gastronomiemarkt in deinem Gebiet. Wir verzichten auf Micromanagement und setzen auf Vertrauen, Freiheit und Ergebnisse.

Deine Mission in Bonn oder Ruhrgebiet

Du übernimmst die volle Verantwortung für dein Vertriebsgebiet und gewinnst die Top-Locations der Stadt für Lightspeed. Dein Erfolg basiert auf einem modernen, holistischen Vertriebsansatz:

  • Digitaler Rückenwind: Wir unterstützen dich aktiv durch Performance Marketing & qualifizierte Leads.

  • Strategische Partnerschaften: Du baust dir ein lokales Netzwerk und ein starkes Empfehlungsmanagement (Referrals) auf.

  • Gezielte Kaltakquise & Walk-ins: Du bist täglich im Markt präsent, besuchst Restaurants, Cafés sowie Bars und überzeugst die Inhaber direkt vor Ort.

  • Full-Cycle-Verantwortung: Du steuerst den gesamten Prozess selbstständig – vom ersten Händedruck über die Produkt-Demo bis zum erfolgreichen Vertragsabschluss.

  • Beratender Verkauf: Du verkaufst nicht nur Software, sondern hilfst Gastronomen partnerschaftlich dabei, ihr Business erfolgreicher zu machen.



Wer du bist (Dein Profil)

  • Ein echter Hunter: Du liebst die Herausforderung der Neukundengewinnung, bist extrem selbstmotiviert und brauchst niemanden, der dir ständig über die Schulter schaut.

  • Kommunikationsstark: Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (essenziell für den Vertrauensaufbau mit lokalen Inhabern) und bringst gute Englischkenntnisse mit.

  • Charismatisch & Resistent: Du besitzt ein sicheres Auftreten, starke Präsentationsfähigkeiten und hast kein Problem damit, in ein volles Restaurant zu gehen und ein Gespräch zu starten.

  • Ehrgeizig: Du willst deinen Erfolg selbst in die Hand nehmen und suchst ein Umfeld, in dem Leistung direkt belohnt wird.

  • Erfahrung: Erste Erfahrung im Vertrieb, Business Development oder in der Gastronomie ist ein Plus – dein Drive und deine Einstellung zählen für uns jedoch am meisten.



Das Angebot – Warum Lightspeed?

  • Attraktives Vergütungspaket: Ein faires Fixgehalt gepaart mit einer ungedeckelten Provision (uncapped Commission) – mit überdurchschnittlich hohem Verdienstpotenzial für Top-Performer.

  • Regelmäßiger Gehalts-Boost: Eine echte Performance-Kultur, bei der dein Gehalt durch das Erreichen von klaren Umsatzmeilensteinen in schnellen Abständen spürbar steigen kann.

  • Sicherer Start: Wir investieren in dich. Freue dich auf einen erstklassigen Onboarding-Monat sowie eine strukturierte Ramp-up-Phase inklusive garantiertem Bonus in den ersten Monaten.

  • Company Equity: Werde durch unser attraktives Aktienprogramm direkt am Erfolg von Lightspeed beteiligt.

  • Lifestyle & Flexibilität: Profitiere von Vertrauensarbeitszeit, einem monatlichen Extra-Budget für Essen/Getränke sowie einem jährlichen Budget für Fitness und Wellness.

  • Team-Power & Kultur: Arbeite in einem großartigen lokalen Team in unserem NRW HQ und feiere unsere Erfolge bei legendären Events

  • Zusatzleistungen: Zuschuss zu deinem ÖPNV-Ticket für NRW sowie professionelle mentale Unterstützung über die Modern Health App.

 

Bewerb dich jetzt!

    En tant que Business Developer, vous serez chargé de prendre contact sur le terrain avec les praticiens de votre zone et leur proposer les solutions Doctolib. Au quotidien, vos responsabilités incluent, mais ne sont pas limitées à :

    • Êtes passionné par la vente et motivé par les défis

    • Êtes diplômé d'une école de commerce, d'une formation en vente ou équivalent universitaire (IUT/ BTS/ Licence commerciale)

    • Entretien avec un recruteur : Un échange pour découvrir votre parcours, vos motivations et évaluer l'adéquation de vos compétences avec nos besoins.

    • Rencontre avec nos Managers : Une exploration de vos compétences à travers des mises en situation concrètes et une présentation de notre équipe et mission.

title: Finance Assistant
descriptionHtml:
Finance Assistant

Edinburgh

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we’re growing fast.


We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgment matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We’re built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend, and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies use Wordsmith. We’ve raised over $80m from leading investors, and we’re building one of the defining companies in legal AI — from our office in Edinburgh.

Why this role is different

You won’t be joining a big, process-heavy finance function. You’ll be one of the first Finance hires, working on a brand new, AI-native ERP system (Rillet) with the freedom to actually improve how things are done — not just keep the lights on.

If you want real exposure to the business, a seat close to the founders and leadership team, and the chance to shape processes rather than inherit them, this is that seat.

The Role

As Finance Assistant, you’ll own the day-to-day mechanics that keep Wordsmith’s finances running — cash, invoicing, collections, payables and expenses — and you’ll have the tools and the licence to automate as much of it as possible.

What you'll do

  • Complete daily cash reconciliation across our accounts

Who you might be

What we're looking for

  • Newly qualified, 1–2 years PQE, or qualified by experience

  • Highly organised, with the judgement to know when something needs chasing

How we work

This role is on-site five days a week, from our office in central Edinburgh — a short walk from both Waverley and Haymarket. You’ll sit inside a small finance team, which means direct exposure to the wider business rather than being several layers removed from it.

It’s a fast-moving environment with light process and a genuine bias toward using technology to remove manual work, not add to it.

What you can expect

Why Wordsmith

We’re a fast-moving, Edinburgh-based Legal AI company that’s just raised over $80m. Joining now means joining early enough to shape how our finance function is built — with modern tools, real ownership, and a team that wants to do things properly rather than just keep pace.

title: Forward deployed engineer, energy
descriptionHtml:
About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

Forward Deployed Energy Engineers are a new role at Watershed, combining energy and advisory expertise with product-building skills and commercial instinct. You’ll operate at the cutting edge with Watershed customers to build and deploy the next generation of enterprise energy management.

Energy is one of the largest costs on a big company’s P&L and one of its largest sources of emissions. Yet most enterprises have no one who owns how energy is purchased, consumed and reduced across all their sites. Watershed is building the product that changes that, and it’s the company’s biggest bet for its next chapter.

We already help many of the world’s largest companies measure and cut their emissions, and our clean energy business has executed more than $100M in purchases. Now we’re building energy management from zero to one, with engagements underway with a small group of customers today and scaling in 2027.

You’ll work with enterprises that spend tens of millions a year on electricity, embedded in their energy programmes. Starting from the energy data already in Watershed, you’ll find where they’re overspending, deliver the savings, prototype with AI what should become product, and help customers implement solutions, including buying clean power. The goal is an energy programme that wins backing from their CFO and facilities teams. This is a high-ownership role on a small, high-output team, with a direct line to commercial outcomes and real say in what we build. It reports directly to Watershed’s head of energy and decarbonization.

What you'll do

  • Deliver energy engagements with measurable results: Run deep engagements with a handful of customers at a time: change tariffs, upgrade equipment, find and cut waste, and show the savings.

  • Win customers who vouch for us: Earn the trust of facilities and finance leads so they would tell a peer to work with Watershed.

  • Turn what works into product: Spot the problems that repeat across customers, prototype with AI, and work with our engineers to build an AI-led product for many.

  • Close clean energy deals: Help customers sign deals with existing clean power products (eg EACs, fixed-price VPPAs), yourself or alongside our account teams.

  • Make the team smarter on energy: Be the person colleagues go to on tariffs, loads and what actually cuts a bill.

You might be a fit if you

  • Know how commercial and industrial sites use and buy energy (tariffs, loads, HVAC and controls, procurement) from time at an ESCO, an energy consultancy, an engineering firm or an energy-tech company.

  • Have built things: scripts, models, prototypes or AI-assisted workflows, and can show us one. Prototype-quality code is enough; moving fast matters most.

  • Are fluent with data tools (Excel, SQL or Python) and LLM tools, and can turn messy meter and bill data into something a customer acts on.

  • Have run client work from scoping to outcome, and are as credible with a facilities manager as with a CFO.

  • Can tell a compelling story with data, from raw numbers to insight to a recommendation someone signs off. You've originated work or supported deals, and want to get better at selling.

  • Are energised to build a new product and service, to be on the front lines of building a new business, and to leave a legacy as part of a fast-moving team.

Nice to have

  • Experience with clean power deals (PPAs, VPPAs, fixed-price power contracts, and energy attribute certificates like RECs, GOs and REGOs).

  • Hands-on work with utility bill, half-hourly or building management system data.

  • A few years in consulting or advisory.

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

Vogel berät mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen in steuerlichen, kaufmännischen und strategischen Fragen. Darauf bauen wir eine Beratungsplattform für den deutschen Mittelstand, organisch und durch Zukäufe, mit einem gemeinsamen Setup, in das jede neue Einheit integriert wird. Vogel ist inhabergeführt, und du arbeitest unmittelbar an den Themen der Geschäftsführung mit.

Du studierst im fortgeschrittenen Bachelor oder im Master oder bist im Gap Year. Die Fachrichtung ist zweitrangig, wichtig ist, dass du herausgestochen bist. Du willst kein Traineeprogramm mit festen Stationen, sondern wissen, wie Entscheidungen tatsächlich entstehen: mit unvollständigen Daten, unter Zeitdruck, zwischen Menschen unterschiedlicher Meinung.

Das Praktikum dauert drei bis sechs Monate in Vollzeit. Du verantwortest ein bis zwei eigene Themen und arbeitest direkt mit der Geschäftsführung.

Deine Verantwortung

Analyse und Entscheidungsvorlagen

  • Du nimmst eine offene Frage der Geschäftsführung, strukturierst sie und lieferst eine Antwort auf zwei Seiten, mit eigener Einschätzung. Dein Maßstab: Wer die Vorlage liest, kann danach entscheiden.

  • Du baust Auswertungen aus unseren Zahlen: Ergebnisse je Einheit, Mandatsstrukturen, Auslastung, Wachstumstreiber. Die Daten holst du selbst, deine Annahmen dokumentierst du mit.

  • Du prüfst Annahmen nach, die im Haus als gesetzt gelten, und stellst sachlich fest, wenn etwas nicht mehr stimmt.

Eigene Themen von der Frage bis zum Ergebnis

  • Du übernimmst eigene Themen über die gesamte Strecke und trägst die Ergebnisse selbst vor der Geschäftsführung vor.

  • Du arbeitest in laufenden Vorhaben quer durch das Unternehmen mit: Integration eines zugekauften Hauses, Aufbau eines neuen Beratungsfelds, Einführung eines Werkzeugs in allen Einheiten.

Interne Steuerung und Kultur

  • Du baust an den Formaten mit, über die das Unternehmen gesteuert wird: Berichtswege, Kennzahlen, Entscheidungsvorlagen, interne Kommunikation.

  • Du verantwortest Anlässe, an denen unsere Kultur konkret wird, von der Town Hall bis zum Sommerfest, gemeinsam mit dem Growth-Team.

  • Du wirkst im Recruiting mit: Sichtung, eigene Einschätzung zu Kandidaten, Mitarbeit am Bewerbungsprozess.

Deine Perspektiven

Was du nach 3 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du hast zwei eigene Themen von der Fragestellung bis zum Ergebnis verantwortet und selbst vorgetragen.

  • Mehrere deiner Entscheidungsvorlagen haben zu tatsächlichen Entscheidungen geführt.

Was du nach 6 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du verantwortest ein eigenes, abgegrenztes Thema, bei dem die Geschäftsführung nicht mehr nachfasst.

  • Die Bereichsleitungen sprechen dich direkt an, wenn sie eine Analyse brauchen.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Du siehst in wenigen Monaten, wie ein wachsendes Unternehmen entscheidet, und nimmst eine Arbeitsweise mit, die in jeder späteren Rolle trägt. Wer überzeugt, bleibt im Gespräch.

Das bringst du mit

Erfahrung & Track Record

  • Ein fortgeschrittener Bachelor oder Master mit sehr guten Leistungen: Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Jura, Naturwissenschaften oder ein Fach, in dem du nachweislich herausgestochen bist.

  • Erste Praxis in einem anspruchsvollen Umfeld ist ein Plus: Beratung, Investment Banking, Private Equity, Scale-up, Founders Office oder eine eigene Gründung.

  • Profile, die nicht in dieses Raster passen, aber Denkschärfe und Umsetzungskraft mitbringen, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du schreibst klar und knapp. Zwei gute Seiten schlagen bei uns zwanzig vollständige.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Recherche, Analyse und Drafting. Repetitive Aufgaben sind für dich ein Anlass zur Automatisierung.

  • Bei einer offen formulierten Aufgabe machst du deine Annahmen explizit, schlägst eine Richtung ein und justierst unterwegs.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du verträgst die direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung: schnelle Iteration, hohe Eigenständigkeit und auch Aufgaben, die nicht im Lebenslauf glänzen.

  • Du bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen. Die Steuerberaterin mit 20 Jahren Erfahrung weiß Dinge über ihr Mandat, die in keinem Modell stehen.

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen, nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Keine Konzern-Strategieabteilung. Was du schreibst, geht in eine Entscheidung, die diese Woche fällt.

  • Keinen Elfenbeinturm. Eine Empfehlung ohne Verantwortung für die Umsetzung ist hier keine Lieferung.

  • Kein Praktikum mit Rotationsplan. Du bekommst eigene Themen und damit auch die Konsequenzen deiner Entscheidungen.

  • Keine Zuarbeit für eine Zwischenebene. Du trägst deine Ergebnisse selbst vor der Geschäftsführung vor.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

Compensation: €4K per month

title: Founding Engineer - Ambient Care Startup
descriptionHtml:
Stage: Pre-seed. Location: Cambridge/London, UK. Comp: Competitive + Equity

About Subtle

Most families find out something's wrong too late: a fall, a missed check-in, a change no one noticed until it became a crisis. We're building ambient sensing for the elderly and vulnerable at home, technology that quietly looks out for the people we love without asking them to wear anything or change how they live. We're early. We're validating with real customers, building the first hardware, and looking for the person who'll help turn this from an idea into a product families can trust with something this personal.

We are building this from scratch inside Founders Factory's studio, with a dedicated pre-seed investment, hands-on studio support across product, design, talent and growth, and a six-month build programme to get from concept to a fundable, in-market product. This venture has secured a major European technology partner. The founding CEO is already in place. We are now looking for the technical other half of the founding team.


The role

You'll be our first engineering hire, working directly with the founder(s) and carrying real authority over what we build and how. It's a hands-on role that spans hardware and software, and a leadership one too, since you'll grow the team that follows you.

Responsibilities

  • Own hardware validation and bench testing end to end, and lead our manufacturing path. Whether that ends up being an outsourced partner or in-house, you're the one validating the sensor platform yourself and making sure whatever we ship has been properly tested before it reaches someone's home. This is safety-relevant, so you'd rather catch a failure on the bench than have it happen in someone's home.

  • Build the software that turns sensor data into something useful. Detection logic, alerting, and the escalation decisions that sit behind them, tested and monitored with the same rigor as the hardware.

  • Navigate the regulatory and security requirements that come with this territory. Certification requirements for embedded systems (software and hardware), and data protection for Personally Identifiable Information (PII), from day one rather than retrofitted later.

  • Grow the team. As we scale past this hire, you'll hire, mentor and lead the engineers who join under you.

What we're looking for

Must have's

  • Early-stage hardware experience. You've taken a hardware product from 0 to 1 in a startup environment, and you're comfortable spanning embedded systems and software.

  • Experience using AI to accelerate how you work, across engineering, prototyping, and the day-to-day operations of running a startup.

  • Experience leading or building a small engineering team, or clearly ready to step into that.

  • A proactive, evidence-first way of working. You're comfortable with ambiguity, and comfortable being told (including by yourself) that a result doesn't hold up.

  • Experience with regulatory, security, or compliance requirements in health tech, medical devices, or another safety- and privacy-regulated space. You understand that building for vulnerable people and their data changes what "done" means.

  • Lead vendor and manufacturing negotiations, securing the right partners, terms, and production capabilities to bring the product to market.

  • Any direct experience taking a regulated product through certification (CE/UKCA, FDA, or equivalent) is considered a major plus.
